lean_implies_paper.reasoning: In the explicit real-square-Frobenius specialization, let dB be the computed-minus-exact right-input perturbation. Then A(B+dB)-AB=A dB, and Lean gives ||A dB||F ≤ ||A||F||dB||F. If err(B,n) is an error bound, ||dB||F ≤ err(B,n) yields the selected contribution ||A||F err(B,n) with coefficient one. This implication concerns P10-T1's selected term, not all of equation (8).

paper_implies_lean.reasoning: Instantiate the paper's normwise right-error amplification rule with real square matrices, the Frobenius norm, and an inherited error matrix dB whose exact error magnitude is ||dB||F. The asserted coefficient-one amplification by the opposite left operand then gives ||A dB||F ≤ ||A||F||dB||F. Universal dB is legitimate because any matrix can serve as a right perturbation; homogeneity also removes any first-order smallness restriction for this isolated linear bound.

rationale: At the granularity of P10-T1, the Lean proposition is the exact algebraic bound that generates equation (8)'s inherited-right-error summand: a right perturbation dB propagates as A dB and has norm at most ||A||F||dB||F. The operand orientation, coefficient one, common size index, absolute normwise character, and absence of ε or μ(n) all match. The real-square-Frobenius choice is an explicit nonvacuous specialization that still supplies the benchmark task, rather than grounds for calling the theorem stronger. The target does not encode the other two terms or the recursive inversion recurrence, but those are outside this selected T1 contribution. Both semantic implications therefore hold for the selected result under the stated specialization.
